security_audit.summary: Of the 21 static matches, only the Leadsets endpoint represents a real network data transfer. The workflow defaults to sending contact identifiers without explicit approval, and its email verification guidance is inconsistent. No evidence of shell execution, environment access, system reconnaissance, or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: The default enrichment run sends contact identifiers to Leadsets without a separate approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Before the first lookup, disclose the service, identifier types, and row count; require approval and send only one necessary identifier per contact.

remediation.issue: The workflow says all enriched emails are verified, despite documenting catch-all and unknown results.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the blanket verification claim and require an explicit verified status. Treat missing or unexpected statuses as unconfirmed and exclude them from verified output.

semantic_findings.title: Default Bulk Sharing Without Explicit Approval
semantic_findings.description: The workflow defaults to the entire list and sends contact identifiers to Leadsets without an explicit approval step. A CRM export can include records the user is not permitted to share.

content.user_title: Detect Job Changes in Your Contact List
content.value_statement: Outdated contact lists make it hard to know who still works in the same role or company. Compare stored records with current Leadsets data and review the changes before updating your CRM.
actual_capabilities: Read a CSV, Google Sheet, or accessible CRM export and remove exact duplicates by email or LinkedIn URL.
Check remaining Leadsets usage and plan batches around account limits.
Compare employer domains and titles to classify company moves, role changes, unchanged contacts, and contacts not found.
Flag old work emails for movers and report new work emails with their returned status when available.
Return a CSV or Google Sheet with change categories, check dates, and a summary of counts and records used.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and either an MCP connection or REST API access.
Requires stored titles, stored companies, and usable contact identifiers. Results depend on Leadsets coverage and freshness.
Processes the supplied contacts only. It does not search for new prospects or send outreach.
CRM write-back requires a separate connection and approval of the exact field changes.

use_cases.title: Review Quarterly CRM Changes
use_cases.description: Review a CRM segment for employer and title changes, then prepare proposed field updates for approval.

use_cases.title: Review a List Before Outreach
use_cases.description: Identify contacts who left their employer and flag old work addresses before using an existing outreach list.

use_cases.title: Track Moves Among Key Contacts
use_cases.description: Check whether key customer contacts moved companies or changed roles before scheduling account reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Small CSV
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Review a short contact list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Leadsets to check this CSV for employer and title changes. Save the results to a new CSV and list any contacts you cannot find.

prompt_templates.title: Review Role and Seniority Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Separate promotions from lateral moves.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Leadsets to check this sheet and separate promotions from other title changes. Treat equivalent title spellings as unchanged and write the results to new tabs.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh a List Within Usage Limits
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Plan a run for a large export.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Leadsets balance and tell me how many contacts from this export you can process now. Check one approved contact first, then process only the contacts I approve. List unfinished rows and report when I can resume.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Proposed CRM Updates
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review field changes before any write.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Leadsets to compare this approved CRM segment by company domain and title. Show the old and new values and the check date for each proposed update. Treat emails without an explicit verified status as unconfirmed. Do not write to the CRM.

output_examples.input: Check my approved CSV of 20 contacts for employer and title changes.
output: Loaded 20 rows and skipped 2 exact duplicates.
Found 3 employer moves, 4 title changes, and 9 unchanged contacts. Leadsets did not find 2 contacts.
Used 16 enrichment records. The CSV flags old work emails for all 3 movers.

output_examples.input: Check this approved list of six account contacts and propose CRM changes.
output: Found 1 employer move, 1 role change, and 4 unchanged contacts.
Alex Lee moved from Cedar Labs to Northview Systems. Leadsets did not return a new work email.
The proposed updates include the old and new values and their check dates. No CRM records were changed.

best_practices: Confirm that you may share the selected contact identifiers with Leadsets before starting.
Start with one approved contact to validate the column mapping and returned data before processing a batch.
Review match dates and email status labels before using the results or approving CRM updates.
anti_patterns: Sending an entire CRM export when you only need to check one segment.
Treating catch-all, unknown, or missing email statuses as verified.
Using a missing match as proof that a contact left the company.

faq.question: Which input formats can I use?
faq.answer: Use a CSV, a Google Sheet, or a CRM export or view that the agent can read.

faq.question: What fields does each contact need?
faq.answer: Include the stored title and company. Provide a LinkedIn URL, a work email, or a full name with a company domain.

faq.question: What contact data goes to Leadsets?
faq.answer: The lookup uses a LinkedIn URL, a work email, or a name with a company domain. Confirm that you have permission to share those identifiers.

faq.question: What happens when I reach my usage limit?
faq.answer: The skill reports completed and pending rows. When Leadsets provides a reset time, the skill tells you when to resume.

faq.question: Is a new work email always verified?
faq.answer: No. Only an explicit verified status counts. Catch-all and unknown results are not verified, and some movers have no new email.

faq.question: Will this update my CRM automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill can propose field changes, but it requires approval of the exact updates before it writes anything to the CRM.
